title: Shock Wave Application to Cell Cultures
protocol: Prepare the IVSWT water bath by filling an appropriate tank with 3.5 L of tap water.
Heat the water to 37 °C and fill the water bath until the level is approximately 3 cm below the edge.
Connect the temperature sensor to the power supply and place it in the fitting on the back wall of the water bath.
Connect heating to the power supply of the temperature sensor once water is present.
Wait for the water to reach a stable temperature of 37 °C.
Stir the water regularly with a stick to ensure constant temperature throughout the water bath.
Seed cells overnight at desired density in T25 culture flasks or culture until they reach the desired confluence before the experiment.
Align the flasks vertically prior to use.
Fill the culture flasks with culture medium until right below their necks.
Screw the flasks with solid caps without filters.
Seal the caps with Parafilm before insertion into the water bath.
Fix sealed culture flasks in the provided stand.
Insert fixed flask into the water bath.
Place the middle of the cell culture flask at the same height as the center of the shock wave applicator's membrane.
Conduct a parameter finding pilot experiment to define treatment parameters.
Define distance between shock wave source and sample.
Choose appropriate treatment parameters (energy flux density, frequency) on the shock wave device.
Apply commercially available ultrasound transmission gel on the shock wave applicator and the membrane of the water bath.
Connect applicator to the membrane and hold it stable in the center of the membrane.
Ensure that the applicator is aligned horizontally.
Make sure that the correct vertical position of the probe inside the water bath is in line with the indicated marking at the side of the bath.
Hold centers of the applicator and the flask stable in a horizontal line.
Activate the shock wave device and apply the impulses while keeping the culture flask as well as the applicator in a stable position during the whole procedure.
Take the culture flask out of the water bath.
Dry it with common paper towels.
Wipe the flask accurately with disinfecting agents.
Remove Parafilm sealing and cap.
Pipette the medium inside the flasks into centrifugal tubes.
Centrifuge appropriately according to the used cell type, e.g., for HUVECs use 290 g at room temperature.
Add 5 ml of cell culture medium to the flask.
Resuspend the centrifuged cell pellet with 2 ml of cell culture medium.
Pipette the suspension into the flask.
Do not connect the heater to the power supply unless the water bath is filled with water to avoid damage.
Use generous amounts of ultrasound gel on the shock wave applicator to ensure proper coupling and wave propagation into the bath.
Check the position of the probes inside the water bath in relation to the applicator to ensure treatment of the entire growth area.
Do not dunk probes too deep into the water to avoid contamination.
